scope: Native Linux x64 actual packaged FIFO owner retained by a root controller, Cargo credential-dropped through maintained supervisor/attached-leader exec, Java compiler wrapper, pinned Rust jobserver importer, then actual rustc exec.

behavior.credentialAccess: Root-owned FIFO published with numeric GID1001 and mode0660. A setpriv uid65534/gid1001 inspector imported it before Cargo; actual dropped Cargo and compiler consumers imported the same owner inode. Only newly owned ancestor directories were assigned required access; every ancestor mode at owner creation remained unchanged after cleanup.
behavior.environment: Map mutation attempt rejected. The exact three leased make-variable strings are passed into LinuxProcessTree.Launch, checked from the held Cargo image /proc environ, and compared against Java wrapper, Rust importer and native rustc exec-child receipts. No environment reconstruction of auth occurs at compiler boundaries.
behavior.capacity: jobs=2: one implicit Cargo slot plus one initially seeded explicit token. Independent workload token inspector observes1 before and after. While A holds its Cargo slot and B has requested another explicit token, B remains blocked and Cargo live. After A completes, B acquires and returns; both produce metadata.
behavior.ordinaryFailure: Changed A to an E0308 type error using retained incremental target. Exactly one persisted wrapper attempt, native compiler exit1, Cargo101, E0308 visible, terminationRequested=false, final explicit count1.
behavior.lifetime: Native rustc status wait, wrapper native-child wait, supervisor complete and close, Cargo/supervisor PIDs absent and owned cgroup absent are established before returning the lease. Owner close then removes FIFO/directory and no live or deleted FIFO descriptor remains in the controller; FD number reuse by unrelated resources is permitted.
behavior.incrementalAndFresh: Fixture, packaged JAR, native library and consumer outputs retained across scratch-driver corrections. Successful incremental case completed first; one separate empty fresh Cargo target then completed with identical manifest/source hashes and same JAR/toolchain/driver. Ordinary failure used the retained incremental target.

failure_diagnostics.stage: First controller attempt, before Cargo launch
failure_diagnostics.rootCause: Scratch Requirements helper supplied a sentence as validator name; Requirements rejects whitespace even for true conditions. Local RequirementsName.java reproduced it; original controller log and source are archived.
failure_diagnostics.repair: Scratch helper first normalized spaces, then a held Cargo credential receipt exposed tab characters in a dynamic name. Final helper uses the fixed identifier condition and preserves descriptive failures in an IOException cause. Packaged owner never changed.

failure_diagnostics.rootCause: Controller deliberately changed its owned top directory to root:GID1001 mode0710. SSH runner consequently lacked permission to create patch files there.
failure_diagnostics.repair: Used the already owned runner-writable input-parts child for transfer and sudo decoding into the controller root; no ancestor permission widening. Failed upload and subsequent empty-decode diagnostics remain in local requests/responses.

failure_diagnostics.rootCause: TTY inserts a bracketed-paste control sequence before the ARCHIVE marker, so the initial newline-anchored regex did not match retained bytes.
failure_diagnostics.repair: Parsed the existing response using one long base64 marker, with SHA256 and every archive-member hash verification. No second download or remote test needed.

warnings: Pinned Frida devkit linker executable-stack warning and JVM stack-guard warning remain visible, matching prior prerequisite evidence; no diagnostic suppression or repair.
limits: This proves one Linux x64 transport/ownership composition with configured capacity2, not the full production Cargo coordinator or memory scheduling.
Compiler wrappers and Rust environment recorder are scratch acceptance fixtures using actual packaged owners/supervisor and actual Cargo/rustc; no maintained wrapper/controller CLI was added.
No allocation blocking, memory admission, memory retry policy, killed-token-holder recovery, token reseeding, Bazel, Windows or macOS gates were exercised or claimed.
An ordinary compiler error was propagated with its diagnostic/code and one attempt; there was no byte-for-byte comparison of every stderr byte.
Hosted workflow conclusion remains failure because its intended exit17 deliberately opened debugging. Remote acceptance passed and all four post cleanup steps succeeded.

cleanup.afterAcceptance: Parent removes registered isolated worktree and local scratch when no longer needed.
